issues.problem: On a case-insensitive file system (macOS APFS and HFS+ defaults, the main Cursor platform), the quarantine still moves a user's own agent whose name is a case variant of a bundle SB ships today. The clause `SB_NAMESPACE.match(key) and shipped_name(name)` tests `(bundle_root / name).is_dir()`. On APFS, SB:Review resolves to host-bundles/cursor/sb:review, so the entry counts as provable and is moved with no content check. This breaks the fix's own contract ('an exact colon name ... never a prefix') and this round's acceptance rule that case variants never move. The clause adds no legitimate cleanup: every colon bundle is already on the exact list (the test asserts it), no silver-* bundle ships today, and an entry SB wrote always has SB's exact case. Linux is not affected. The moves are reversible (quarantine, with a Note line). Rated major only because this round's acceptance rule says case variants must never move; otherwise it would be minor like the earlier quarantine findings.

issues.suggested_fix: Make the bundle check exact-case: build `shipped_dirs = {p.name for p in bundle_root.iterdir() if p.is_dir()}` once and test `name in shipped_dirs`. Better, limit that clause to hyphenated silver-* names, since colon names are fully covered by SHIPPED_COLON_NAMES. Add a fixture: a user agent SB:Review/ with sb:review shipped stays. issues.problem: committed() returns False whenever git fails, and it inherits GIT_DIR/GIT_WORK_TREE from the installer's environment. A file the project commits is then moved, although the contract says it never moves. Two ways in: 'detected dubious ownership' (a repo owned by another UID, common with devcontainer and Docker bind mounts, git >= 2.35.2), and an exported GIT_DIR (an installer run from a git hook). With git missing, the inner script dies with a FileNotFoundError traceback after part of the user scope has already been moved. In practice the project root is REPO_ROOT (the SB checkout), which tracks no .cursor/agents, so exposure is small.
issues.evidence: Probe /tmp/claude-0/-home-user-silver-bullet/a8e36ab4-d9e2-56b2-b366-31e100f031d9/scratchpad/review/REVF-H2-r4-probe/q3 runs the project with a tracked sb:plan/ dir, a tracked sb:review.md, a staged sb:debug.md and an untracked sb:spec.md. (L) `chown -R nobody prj; GIT_CONFIG_NOSYSTEM=1 run.sh` -> all 4 quarantined, tracked files included. (M) `GIT_DIR=<other repo>/.git run.sh` -> all 4 quarantined. (N) PATH without git -> 'FileNotFoundError: [Errno 2] No such file or directory: git' traceback. Baseline: the 3 tracked or staged entries stay.
issues.suggested_fix: Run git with GIT_DIR, GIT_WORK_TREE and GIT_INDEX_FILE removed from env. Treat only 'not a git repository' (rc 128 with that message, or `git rev-parse --is-inside-work-tree` false) as untracked, and keep the entry with a Note on any other git failure, including FileNotFoundError. Add a dubious-ownership or GIT_DIR test.

issues.problem: The new repair step adds a second config.toml writer in its own python process, but the uninstall never exports SB_INSTALL_RUN_START. Whether the purge keeps the repair's backup (the original file) therefore depends on the 2 s margin from _PROCESS_START. When the purge starts more than 2 s after the repair wrote the backup, the .sb-backup becomes the intermediate repaired file. With only one writer before this delta, the backup was always the original. The installers export the variable; this path does not. Only SB's own duplicated tables are lost from the backup.
issues.evidence: Probe /tmp/claude-0/-home-user-silver-bullet/a8e36ab4-d9e2-56b2-b366-31e100f031d9/scratchpad/review/REVF-H2-r4-probe/un with a python3 shim that sleeps 3 s before exec (PATH=/tmp/claude-0/-home-user-silver-bullet/a8e36ab4-d9e2-56b2-b366-31e100f031d9/scratchpad/review/REVF-H2-r4-probe/un/slow:$PATH): uninstall rc=0, but `diff orig.toml config.toml.sb-backup` shows the second [hooks.state."silver-bullet@...:0:0"] / trusted_hash = "sha256:b" missing.
